Question: A function \(f\) has domain \([0, 2]\) and range \([0, 1].\) (The notation \([a, b]\) denotes \(\{x : a \le x \le b\}.\)) What are the domain and range, respectively, of the function \(g\) defined by \[g(x) = 1 - f(x + 1)?\]
Solution:
The expression \(f(x+1)\) is defined exactly when its input \(x+1\) belongs to the domain of \(f\). Thus
\[
0\le x+1\le2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-1\le x\le1.
\]
So the domain of \(g\) is \([-1,1]\).

As \(x\) runs through this interval, \(x+1\) runs through every input in \([0,2]\). Therefore \(f(x+1)\) attains every value \(y\) in \([0,1]\), and no others. The resulting output \(1-y\) lies in \([0,1]\). Moreover, every \(z\in[0,1]\) is obtained by choosing \(y=1-z\), which is an attained value of \(f\). Hence the range is exactly \([0,1]\), including both endpoints.

The domain and range are \([-1,1]\) and \([0,1]\), respectively, choice B.
